[[BEC Tero Sasana FC|BEC Tero Sasana]] | highest scoring = [[TOT FC|TOT]] '''3-6''' [[Rattana Bundit FC|Bangkok Metropolitan Administration]] (9 goals) | total goals = | average goals = | longest wins = | longest unbeaten = | longest losses = | highest attendance = | lowest attendance = | average attendance = | prevseason = [[1999 Thai Premier League|1999]] | nextseason = [[2001–02 Thai League|2001–02]] }} The '''2000 [[Thai Premier League]]''' consisted of 12 teams. The bottom club would be relegated to the [[Thailand Division 1 League]]. The club that came 11th would play in a relegation / promotion match against the club that came second in the Thailand Division 1 League. Champions [[Royal Thai Air Force]] entered the next edition of the [[Asian Club Championship]]. |update=complete|source=[https://www.rsssf.org/tablest/thai00.html rsssf.com] |class_rules=1st points; 2nd head-to-head; 3rd goal difference; 4th goals scored }} ==Promotion and relegation playoff== The club that came 11th in the [[Thai Premier League]] was to play in a relegation / promotion match against the runner-up in the [[Thailand Division 1 League]], but at the end of the season, [[Thai Farmers Bank FC|Thai Farmers Bank]] dropped out of the league and folded. As such, [[Chula-Sinthana FC|Sinthana]], the club that came 11th, took their place, while [[TOT FC|TOT]], the team that came 12th, would play in the relegation / promotion match. March 27 and March 31, 2001 {| border="1" cellpadding="4" cellspacing="0" style="text-align:center; border-collapse:collapse;" |- style="background:#efefef;" ! Team 1 ! Result ! Team 2 |- style="" | † [[TOT FC|TOT]] | 4-0 | [[Bangkok Christian College FC|Bangkok Christian College]] |} † [[TOT FC|TOT]] remain in the [[Thai Premier League]]. ==Season notes== [[Thai Farmers Bank FC|Thai Farmers Bank]] would withdraw from the league at the end of the season due to the Asian financial crisis that initial struck in 1998. The effects would spread across Asia and many clubs now came under a huge financial burden. ==Queen's Cup== [[Bangkok Bank FC|Bangkok Bank]] won the 27th edition of the [[Queen's Cup (football)|Queen's Cup]] and their third title overall. They defeated [[Sinthana FC|Sinthana]] 5–3 on penalties after a 2–2 draw played at [[Suphachalasai Stadium]]. ==Thailand FA Cup== [[BEC Tero Sasana FC|BEC Tero Sasana]] won their first [[Thailand FA Cup]]. It is unclear whom they beat in the final. ==Asian Representation== * [[Royal Thai Air Force FC|Royal Thai Air Force]] would progress to the second round of the [[2000–01 Asian Club Championship]], but only on the virtue of receiving a bye in the first round. Here, they would get beat once again by [[PSM Ujungpandang]] of Indonesia. * [[BEC Tero Sasana FC|BEC Tero Sasana]] reached the Quarter-finals of the [[2000–01 Asian Cup Winners Cup]], where they were beaten by [[Shimizu S-Pulse]] of Japan in a match played over two legs. They drew the first leg at home, but were overcome in Japan. ==Annual awards== ===Coach of the Year=== *{{flagicon|Thailand}} [[Pichai Pituwong]] - [[BEC Tero Sasana FC|BEC Tero Sasana]] ===Player of the year=== *{{flagicon|Thailand}} [[Anurak Srikerd]] - [[BEC Tero Sasana FC|BEC Tero Sasana]] ===Top scorer=== *{{flagicon|Thailand}} [[Sutee Suksomkit]] - 16 Goals[[Football records in Thailand]] [[Thai Farmers Bank FC|Thai Farmers Bank]] ==Champions== The league champion was [[BEC Tero Sasana]].
